answer: Each identity docks at a jetty under one funding key in a haven registry. The jetty clerk charges a terrace price: the k-th identity pays 70 plus 40 per earlier identity, so the first pays 70 and the thousandth 40,030. Bonds are key-bound, so one covers one identity, and 1,000 fakes cost 20,050,000 credits. Splitting keys fails: a new key cannot sponsor until it has finished one verified epoch, so split registrations wait uncounted. An honest agent pays 70 once and reclaims it after a clean epoch. A rented-key ring fails when an auditor recounts the registry and burns underpaid bonds.
